# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-16 (Extended v126)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter/Spring Year 4—Louis Philippe's reign)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens; le Petit-Picpus convent; M. Gillenormand's residences; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick, Wilholt, Quenford). **Environmental details**: Rain threatened since morning, held off. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Light went early. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Icy breeze; wind off water carries salt/tar scent. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. Children chased hoop down lane, shrieking. **Spring condition**: River up. Weather subject of common conversation.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid, sordid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, obscene charcoal sketches, repulsive moisture. Fireplace with brazier filled burning charcoal (glowing hot, red with blue flame), pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (sleeping woman/child, eagle, Napoleon on blue column). **Wooden panel—Battle of Waterloo painting: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy) amid smoke.** Two heaps: old iron/ropes and rope-ladder with wooden rungs and two hooks. Verdigris candlestick with burning candle.

## Crisis at Gorbeau House: Resolution
**M. Leblanc's binding and struggle**: Overturned furniture, moved toward window with agility. Six robust fists seized him; female Thénardier wound hands in hair. Knocked old man tumbling, swept back two more. Four seized him by both arms and neck. Despite binding, remained impassive—soul inaccessible to terror, preserved silence, forgot anxiety for own life. **Marius found this composure deeply troubling.**

**Thénardier's metamorphosis and scheme**: Transformed from ferocious robber into polished negotiator. Wife to dress as before, hunt up "the Lark" (Cosette) with letter from M. Leblanc. Girl will follow into carriage; outside barrier, trap with two horses waits. Young lady will alight from fiacre; Thénardier's comrade will enter other vehicle with her; wife returns to report completion. **Threat**: "If you have me arrested, my comrade will give a turn of his thumb to the Lark." Thénardier avoided naming girl—precaution of clever man.

**M. Leblanc's extraordinary escape (turning point)**: Before seven men could act, M. Leblanc bent into fireplace, stretched hand to brazier, straightened himself up. **Brandished above his head the red-hot chisel, emitting threatening glow**—almost free and in formidable attitude. All huddled in amazement and stupefaction. Had concealed coin piece when searched; contrived to keep it in hand; unscrewed it and used as saw to cut cords—explaining faint noise Marius had observed. While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, **impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty.**

**Javert's ambush and final escape**: Javert (tall man, square face, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers) positioned outside Gorbeau house with men. Posted young girls as lookouts; "caged" Azelma—Éponine disappeared. Grew impatient, decided upstairs without waiting for Marius's pistol-shot signal. Took action before Marius fired. Ruffians terrified, flung themselves on abandoned arms—one with meat-axe, another with key, another with bludgeon, rest with shears, pincers, hammers. Thénardier had knife. **Thénardier woman snatched enormous paving-stone, hurled at Javert's head. Javert ducked; stone struck wall behind.** **M. Leblanc's escape during chaos**: Door guarded, but window was not. As soon as released from bonds, took advantage of confusion, crowd, darkness, moment when attention diverted, to dash out window.

## Marius Pontmercy: Crisis of Conscience (Unresolved)
**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen. **Now recognized**: Thénardier depicted in Waterloo painting—sergeant who rescued father at Waterloo.

**Unprecedented perplexity**: For last hour had two voices in conscience—one enjoining respect for father's testament, other crying to rescue prisoner. Two voices continued uninterrupted struggle tormenting him to agony. **Had not time for deliberation—scene hastening to catastrophe. Knees gave way. Last possibility of doubt vanished. Certainly was Thénardier of the will.**

**Critical moral dilemma**: Everything depended on Marius. He held all beings in hand. If he fired pistol, M. Leblanc saved, Thénardier lost; if he did not, M. Leblanc sacrificed. Remorse awaited either case. Father once saved by Thénardier at Waterloo. Yet M. Leblanc now victim of Thénardier's ambush. Moral obligation to both: honor father's will AND prevent crime against innocent man and Cosette's father. **Crisis at absolute peak; outcome unclear.**

## Girl (Cosette) and M. Leblanc Identity
**Girl identity clarified**: Handkerchief bore letters U. F., meaning Urbain Fabre. M. Leblanc is Monsieur Fabre—the girl's biological father. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. **Marius recognizes**: The "girl" he worshipped six months is Cosette, whom he encountered again in hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc. She is being held captive by Thénardier's scheme.

## Jean Valjean
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence.

## English Provincial Towns: Population Movements and Mundane Activities
**Population movements**: Peten Haskick broke faith with Luwyn Brackick; promised work never begun. Peten found work in Quenford, moved there, did not return to Staveford. Lura Haskick followed him within the month. Kadrek went to live in Wilholt. Only daughter of Zalis Corrley left Torton, settled in Wilholt. Before spring, Kadan Corrley took Yewyn Corrford in marriage at Kelmere; lived there from then on. In chapel at Ostcombe, Quiet Jotho married eldest daughter of Fewyn Stenworth; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. **That spring, coughing sickness took Nelan; he was buried at Kelford.** Stenworth and Prydenridge families: Pelde Stenson, Davus Stenworth, Fewyn Stenworth, Havus Stenworth, Havie Prydenridge, Dalis, Yera Stenworth, Nerine Prydenridge, Luvie Prydenridge, Zavus Prydenridge, Vesmira Thornmere, Wenelle Lindmere (gave up idleness, took work as chandler), Isric Thornmere, Jotho Thornmere.

**Daily activities**: Sorting old letters, mending torn sleeves, scrubbing steps, humming childhood tunes. Fewyn Stenworth and Rorald argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Pelia Lindmere and Havie Prydenridge read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Pelia and Rovus Prydenridge hummed childhood tunes while scrubbing steps. Jotho Thornmere spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Zavus Prydenridge walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Nerine mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Volan watched clouds and predicted rain (wrongly). Weather and harvest subject of constant conversation. "I heard the river is up again," Volia Brackick remarked; Vlan Stenworth said it always was in spring. "Will it rain, do you think?" asked Volan Stenworth. Volia Brackick only shrugged.

## Historical Context: The Restoration, Revolution of July, and Philosophical Implications (1815-1832)
**Bourbon Restoration critique**: After Napoleon fell, House of Bourbon returned. Believed it bestowed rights and could take back charter rights. Did not suspect roots of French society not fixed in Bourbons but in nations. Bourbons were illustrious knot in history, but no longer principal element of destiny.

**Restoration's fatal decision (1830)**: Abruptly decided plan of action and risked its stroke. Contested collective title and individual right of nation to sovereignty, of citizen to liberty. Denied to nation that which made it a nation.

**Fifteen years of intellectual progress (1815-1830)**: Nation had grown accustomed to calm discussion, to grandeur in peace. Great principles—equality before law, liberty of conscience, speech, press, accessibility of all aptitudes to all functions—could be seen at work in perfect peace until 1830. **The Bourbons were instrument of civilization which broke in hands of Providence.**

**Revolution of July (1830)**: Hardly produced shock; did not treat vanquished royalty as enemy, shedding blood. In eyes of despotic governments, committed fault of being formidable while remaining gentle. Mysterious respect springs from events in which we sense collaboration of someone working above man.

**Philosophical reflection on Right vs. Fact**: Property of right is to remain eternally beautiful and pure. Fact, if containing only too little right or none, infallibly destined to become deformed, impure, perhaps monstrous. **Revolutions vs. revolts**: Old legitimist parties assailed Revolution of 1830 with vehemence from false reasoning. Errors strike it cleverly in vulnerable spot, in default of cuirass, in lack of logic. Attacked this revolution in its royalty, shouted: "Revolution, why this king?" Factions are blind men who aim correctly.

**Post-1830 necessities**: Royalty of July obliged to take precedence of all Europe to keep peace. Armed peace reared up despite European cabinet harness. Metternich would gladly have put it in kicking-straps. Pushed on by progress, it pushed on monarchies. After being towed, undertook to tow.

**Social fermentation (Spring Year 4)**: Within society, pauperism, proletariat, salary, education, penal servitude, prostitution, fate of woman, wealth, misery, production, consumption, division, exchange, coin, credit, rights of capital and labor—all questions multiplied above society, terrible slope. Soil (people) traversed by revolutionary currents trembled with indescribably vague epileptic shocks. Thinkers meditated in pacified but profound manner; impassive miners tranquilly pushed galleries into depths of volcano. **Towards end of April, everything aggravated. Fermentation entered boiling state. Ever since 1830, petty partial revolts suppressed, but ever bursting forth afresh—sign of vast underlying conflagration.** France kept eye on Paris; Paris kept eye on Faubourg Saint-Antoine. Government purely and simply called in question. Back shops where workingmen sworn to hasten into street at first cry of alarm, "fight without counting enemy." A man seated in wine-shop corner "assumed sonorous tone," said, "You understand! You have sworn!"

**Socialist theories and economic solutions**: Thinkers raised material questions—agriculture, industry, commerce—almost to dignity of religion. Men designated by generic title "socialists" endeavored to pierce rock of civilization and cause it to spout forth living waters of human felicity. **England creates wealth admirably, divides it badly**—leads to monstrous opulence and wretchedness. All enjoyments for some, all privations for rest; privilege, exception, monopoly, feudalism born from toil. False and dangerous situation, badly constituted grandeur with material elements and no moral element. **Communism and agrarian law mistaken**—their division kills production. Equal partition abolishes emulation and labor. Slaying wealth not same as dividing it. **Solution requires both problems solved**: Encourage wealthy, protect poor, suppress misery, put bridle on unjust jealousy, adjust salary to labor fraternally, mingle education with childhood growth, make science base of manliness, develop minds while keeping arms busy, render property democratic by making it universal, every citizen proprietor. Then: moral and material greatness worthy to call itself France.

**Louis Philippe (Winter Year 4)**: Handsome in old age, remained graceful; not always approved by nation, always by masses; he pleased. Lacked majesty; wore no crown although king, no white hair although old man. Manners of old regime; habits of new—mixture of noble and bourgeois suited 1830. Incorruptible by sacristans, whippers-in, ballet-dancers—part of bourgeois popularity. Had no heart. Went out with umbrella under arm. Bit of mason, gardener, something of doctor; bled postilion who fell from horse. No more went without lancet than Henri IV. without poniard. Royalists jeered—first king to shed blood with object of healing. **Policy more domestic than national. Rather too much paternal king; family incubation to found dynasty afraid of everything; excessive timidity displeasing to people.** Had 14th of July in civil and Austerlitz in military tradition. **Deep tenderness toward family deserved by family. Domestic group worthy of admiration. One daughter, Marie d'Orleans, placed race among artists. Two daughters elicited from Metternich: "They are young people such as rarely seen, and princes such as never seen."** Memory of Revolution like living imprint. **Press free, tribune free, conscience and speech free. Left throne exposed to light. History will do justice for this loyalty.** **What can be said: Louis Philippe, taken in himself and from point of view of human goodness, will remain one of best princes who ever sat on throne.** Moment has not come to pronounce definite judgment. Moments when strong and courageous as he was, overwhelmed by difficulties of being king.

**Cloud gathering (Spring Year 4)**: Piles of shadows covered horizon. Strange shade gradually drew nearer, extended over men, things, ideas—shade from wraths and systems. Everything hastily stifled moving and fermenting. Conscience of honest man resumed breathing; discomfort of air in which sophisms intermingled with truths. Spirits trembled in social anxiety like leaves at storm approach. Electric tension such that first comer, stranger, brought light. Then twilight obscurity closed in again. Deep and dull mutterings allowed judgment of quantity of thunder contained by cloud.
